newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Poll suggests most in HK against dilution of laws.
newsitem.headline: Poll suggests most in HK against dilution of laws.

text.p: Most Hong Kong people appear to be against China's plan to roll back civil liberties when the territory returns to Chinese rule in July, an opinion survey has found.
The telephone poll, by the independent watchdog Hong Kong Policy Viewers, found 54.8 percent of 573 respondents were against Beijing's proposal, survey organisers said on Sunday.
A China-anointed Preparatory Committee on Saturday approved a proposal to repeal or amend a number of laws in Hong Kong, including its Bill of Rights.
The poll found only 17.8 percent supported the move.
"(The poll result shows) Hong Kong people treasure their freedom of speech and assembly," watchdog chairman Wong Cheong-wing told reporters.
The survey, carried out last week, found 58.6 percent of respondents were pessimistic about human rights protection in Hong Kong after the handover.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.
The 150-member Preparatory Committee is responsible for shaping the future of Hong Kong. Its proposal now goes to the Chinese National People's Congress for ratification in March.
